subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker instance create/list/delete/update commands, or should multi-instance Docker remain documented manual Compose/profile operation for now?
rationale: The requested change defines new official operator UX and persistent lifecycle semantics across Docker, config/state/workspace roots, ports, Compose names, update, deletion, and sandbox boundaries; source inspection shows no existing implementation to clean up or narrow automatically.

options.title: Sponsor a core Docker lifecycle
options.body: Approve a minimal explicit core design for named Docker instances, including identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

options.title: Keep manual primitives for now
options.body: Leave this issue open as a design backlog item while relying on the current multi-gateway docs, environment variables, Docker setup script, container targeting, and ClawDock helpers.

options.title: Route to wrapper or ClawHub package
options.body: Decline core ownership unless a missing core API is identified, and ask contributors to maintain a wrapper or package around the current primitives.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core Docker lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve a minimal explicit core design for named Docker instances, including identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the multi-gateway guide, Docker reliability work, and setup product boundary points to steipete for the product-direction call.
